name: ProteinBench against ProteinGym on ESM-IF1 and ProteinMPNN: different tasks

attributes.rationale: ProteinBench measures sequence design on de novo backbones of length 100 to 500, scored by pLDDT and scTM after refolding, the task ProteinMPNN was built for. Every consensus comparison is ProteinGym zero-shot variant effect prediction (DMS Spearman, clinical AUC), where ESM-IF1 scores 0.422 against ProteinMPNN's 0.257. Design quality and variant scoring are different endpoints; both sets of results are kept as reported. The high severity comes from the strong-consensus step cancelling the cross-task step (issue 201).

name: mRNABench against non-coding RNA benchmarks on DNABERT-2 and RNA-FM: different sequence domain

attributes.rationale: mRNABench probes frozen embeddings on mature mRNA properties (half-life, ribosome load, localisation, eCLIP, GO terms, variant effects). The consensus is Wang et al. 2026 zero-shot non-coding RNA tasks (RNAGym ncRNA DMS, Rfam families, ArchiveII RNA types) and You et al. 2026 fine-tuned splice-site classification. RNA-FM was trained on non-coding RNA; DNABERT-2 on whole genomes. Three of the seven mRNABench wins are 1.2 to 2.7 percent apart and no error bars are reported. RNA-FM's input length limit, which would truncate most full-length mRNAs, has not yet been checked (issue 202).

name: Livesey and Marsh 2025 on Eigen and MutationAssessor: DMS against clinical endpoints

attributes.rationale: Livesey and Marsh rank MutationAssessor above Eigen on their DMS benchmarks (pairwise Spearman win rate, for example 58.8 against 52.4 over 36 DMS sets) but Eigen above MutationAssessor on their own clinical benchmark (54.6 against 51.4), agreeing with the consensus. Every consensus study is clinical or cancer classification: Cubuk 2021 BRCA functional calls, Chen 2020 driver mutations, Lee 2026 CGC oncogenicity. The split between functional-assay and clinical endpoints is the reason; all results are kept as reported.

name: Wu et al. 2025 on Geneformer and scGPT: annotation transfer against embedding quality

attributes.rationale: Wu et al. 2025 measure cross-atlas cell-type annotation transfer (Tabula Sapiens and HLCA, 14 shared cell types, OnClass on zero-shot embeddings), where Geneformer wins 3 of 4. About 200 of the roughly 215 consensus results come from one study, Kedzierska et al. 2025, scoring zero-shot cell embeddings with scIB metrics across several scGPT checkpoints and one Geneformer. Different task; all results kept as reported. The consensus count reflects result rows, not independent studies (issues 201 and 206).

name: Guille et al. 2025 on DeepSomatic and somatic caller ensembles: different ensembles compared as one system

attributes.rationale: The consensus system pools Hasan 2026's majority-vote, union and strict-intersection ensembles of Mutect2, Strelka2 and DeepSomatic, and Guille 2025's vote ensembles that do not include DeepSomatic. Taking each system's best value per metric uses the union for recall and the intersection for precision, and both contain DeepSomatic, so the consensus beats DeepSomatic by construction. The rule compared systems that are not the same (issue 204).

name: RNAGym leaderboard against Wang et al. 2026 on RNAErnie and AIDO.RNA: same assays, opposite order

attributes.rationale: Both sides score the RNAGym ncRNA DMS assays. name: Brandes et al. 2023 against ProteinGym clinical on ESM-1b and EVE

attributes.rationale: Brandes 2023, the ESM-1b developers' paper, ranks ESM-1b above EVE on ClinVar missense (global ROC-AUC 0.892 against 0.883); ProteinGym's clinical substitutions benchmark ranks EVE above ESM-1b (average AUC 0.914 against 0.892). ESM-1b's score is the same in both; only EVE's differs. Working hypothesis: global AUC across genes against per-gene average AUC, and different variant sets. Being checked (issue 211).
